{
  "extract_plan": {
    "chunk_summary": "NIST AI RMF §§3.2–3.5 characterize trustworthy AI: safety (quoting ISO/IEC TS 5723:2022), security and resilience, accountability and transparency, and explainability and interpretability."
  },
  "concepts": [
    {
      "id": "n_ai_safety",
      "name": "AI safety",
      "aliases": ["safety", "safe AI systems"],
      "description": "Operation of AI systems that does not endanger human life, health, property, or the environment; improved through responsible design, deployment practices, simulation and in-domain testing, monitoring, and human intervention.",
      "anchor": "practical approaches for AI safety",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_safety_risks",
      "name": "safety risks",
      "aliases": ["AI safety risk"],
      "description": "Risks of AI systems leading to injury, death, or other endangerment; prioritized by context and severity.",
      "anchor": "Different types of safety risks",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_ai_risk_management",
      "name": "AI risk management",
      "aliases": ["risk management process"],
      "description": "Tailored approaches to managing AI risk, whose urgency and thoroughness scale with the severity of potential harm and which should align with sector-specific guidance.",
      "anchor": "tailored AI risk management approaches",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_resilience",
      "name": "resilience",
      "aliases": ["resilient AI systems"],
      "description": "Ability of an AI system and its ecosystem to withstand unexpected adverse events or changes, maintain function and structure, degrade safely, and return to normal function.",
      "anchor": "Security and resilience are related",
      "location": "3.3 Secure and Resilient"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_security",
      "name": "security",
      "aliases": ["secure AI systems", "AI security"],
      "description": "Maintenance of confidentiality, integrity, and availability through protection mechanisms preventing unauthorized access and use; encompasses resilience plus protocols to avoid, protect against, respond to, and recover from attacks.",
      "anchor": "security includes",
      "location": "3.3 Secure and Resilient"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_transparency",
      "name": "transparency",
      "aliases": ["Transparency"],
      "description": "Extent to which information about an AI system and its outputs is available to individuals interacting with it, tailored to lifecycle stage and to the role or knowledge of AI actors.",
      "anchor": "Meaningful transparency provides",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_accountability",
      "name": "accountability",
      "aliases": ["Accountability"],
      "description": "Answerability for the outcomes of AI systems; presupposes transparency and varies across cultural, legal, sectoral, and societal contexts.",
      "anchor": "seeking accountability",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_explainability",
      "name": "explainability",
      "aliases": ["Explainability"],
      "description": "Representation of the mechanisms underlying an AI system's operation; answers how a decision was made.",
      "anchor": "lack of explainability",
      "location": "3.5 Explainable and Interpretable"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_interpretability",
      "name": "interpretability",
      "aliases": ["Interpretability"],
      "description": "Meaning of an AI system's output in the context of its designed functional purpose; answers why a decision was made and what it means to the user.",
      "anchor": "Risks to interpretability",
      "location": "3.5 Explainable and Interpretable"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_ai_actors",
      "name": "AI actors",
      "aliases": ["AI developers and deployers"],
      "description": "Parties whose role is considered when seeking accountability for AI system outcomes and to whom transparency is tailored.",
      "anchor": "The role of AI actors",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "n_training_data_provenance",
      "name": "provenance of training data",
      "aliases": ["training data provenance"],
      "description": "Maintenance of the origin record of training data, and attribution of system decisions to subsets of it, as an aid to transparency and accountability.",
      "anchor": "Maintaining the provenance of training data",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [
    {
      "id": "d_secure",
      "term": "secure",
      "verbatim_text": "AI systems that can maintain confidentiality, integrity, and availability through protection mechanisms that prevent unauthorized access and use may be said to be secure",
      "normative_status": "standard",
      "as_of_date": null,
      "anchor": "to be secure",
      "location": "3.3 Secure and Resilient"
    },
    {
      "id": "d_explainability",
      "term": "Explainability",
      "verbatim_text": "Explainability refers to a representation of the mechanisms underlying AI systems",
      "normative_status": "standard",
      "as_of_date": null,
      "anchor": "Explainability refers to",
      "location": "3.5 Explainable and Interpretable"
    },
    {
      "id": "d_interpretability",
      "term": "interpretability",
      "verbatim_text": "interpretability refers to the meaning of AI systems’ output in the context of their designed functional purposes",
      "normative_status": "standard",
      "as_of_date": null,
      "anchor": "interpretability refers to",
      "location": "3.5 Explainable and Interpretable"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "cl_safe_iso",
      "claim_text": "AI systems should “not under defined conditions, lead to a state in which human life, health, property, or the environment is endangered”",
      "claim_type": "normative",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "the environment is endangered",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_severe_safety_priority",
      "claim_text": "Safety risks that pose a potential risk of serious injury or death call for the most urgent prioritization and most thorough risk management process.",
      "claim_type": "normative",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "most urgent prioritization",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_early_safety_design",
      "claim_text": "Employing safety considerations during the lifecycle and starting as early as possible with planning and design can prevent failures or conditions that can render a system dangerous.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "render a system dangerous",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_sector_alignment",
      "claim_text": "AI safety risk management approaches should take cues from efforts and guidelines for safety in fields such as transportation and healthcare, and align with existing sector- or application-specific guidelines or standards.",
      "claim_type": "normative",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "take cues from efforts",
      "location": "3.2 Safe"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_security_resilience_distinct",
      "claim_text": "Security and resilience are related but distinct characteristics.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "related but distinct characteristics",
      "location": "3.3 Secure and Resilient"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_resilience_robustness",
      "claim_text": "Resilience relates to robustness and goes beyond the provenance of the data to encompass unexpected or adversarial use (or abuse or misuse) of the model or data.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "goes beyond the provenance",
      "location": "3.3 Secure and Resilient"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_trustworthy_accountability",
      "claim_text": "Trustworthy AI depends upon accountability.",
      "claim_type": "normative",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "depends upon accountability",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_accountability_presupposes",
      "claim_text": "Accountability presupposes transparency.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "presupposes transparency",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_transparent_not_sufficient",
      "claim_text": "A transparent system is not necessarily an accurate, privacy-enhanced, secure, or fair system.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "not necessarily an accurate",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_severe_consequences_adjust",
      "claim_text": "When consequences are severe, such as when life and liberty are at stake, AI developers and deployers should consider proportionally and proactively adjusting their transparency and accountability practices.",
      "claim_type": "normative",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "life and liberty are at stake",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_provenance_assists",
      "claim_text": "Maintaining the provenance of training data and supporting attribution of the AI system’s decisions to subsets of training data can assist with both transparency and accountability.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "can assist with both transparency",
      "location": "3.4 Accountable and Transparent"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_explainable_debuggable",
      "claim_text": "Explainable systems can be debugged and monitored more easily, and they lend themselves to more thorough documentation, audit, and governance.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "debugged and monitored more easily",
      "location": "3.5 Explainable and Interpretable"
    },
    {
      "id": "cl_three_characteristics",
      "claim_text": "Transparency, explainability, and interpretability are distinct characteristics that support each other.",
      "claim_type": "empirical",
      "evidence_grade": "practitioner_assertion",
      "anchor": "distinct characteristics that support",
      "location": "3.5 Explainable and Interpretable"
    }
  ],
